PUBLICAT ÎN PESTE 30 DE ȚĂRI

Ea este opusul lui în orice privință… și cea mai mare ispită pe care el a cunoscut-o vreodată.

Rezervat și mereu stăpân pe el, îmbrăcat tot timpul la patru ace, Kai Young nu are nici timp, nici chef de haos în viața lui. Iar Isabella, cu pletele ei violete și glumele ei nerușinate, pare întruchiparea haosului.

În așteptarea votului pentru poziția de CEO al unui imperiu mass-media, moștenitorul miliardar nu-și permite distrageri precum Isabella. Ea este tot ce n-ar trebui să-și dorească, dar cu fiecare privire aruncată în direcția ei și cu fiecare atingere, Kai este din ce în ce mai tentat să calce în picioare toate regulile… și s-o facă numai a lui.

Îndrăzneață, impulsivă și plină de viață, Isabella Valencia se împacă bine cu toată lumea și până acum nu a întâlnit niciun tip pe care să nu-l poată seduce… cu excepția lui Kai Young. Dar asta n-ar trebui să conteze. El oricum nu este genul ei. Kai traduce clasici în latină ca un simplu hobby, iar faptul că este un membru al clubului unde ea lucrează ca barmaniță înseamnă că nu pot avea o relație.

Însă Isabella nu poate să nege că, dincolo de aspectul lui glacial, Kai este un bărbat care ar putea s-o facă să se topească printr-o simplă atingere.

Indiferent cât de tare se străduiesc, cei doi nu-și pot înăbuși dorința de a fi împreună.

Chiar dacă îi costă totul.

She's his opposite in every way...and the greatest temptation he's ever known.

Reserved, controlled, and proper to a fault, Kai Young has neither the time nor inclination for chaos—and Isabella, with her purple hair and inappropriate jokes, is chaos personified.

With a crucial CEO vote looming and a media empire at stake, the billionaire heir can’t afford the distraction she brings.

Isabella is everything he shouldn’t want, but with every look and every touch, he’s tempted to break all his rules…and claim her as his own.

***

Bold, impulsive, and full of life, Isabella Valencia has never met a party she doesn’t like or a man she couldn’t charm...except for Kai Young.

It shouldn’t matter. He’s not her type—the man translates classics into Latin for fun, and his membership at the exclusive club where she bartends means he’s strictly off limits.

But she can’t deny that, beneath his cool exterior, is a man who could make her melt with just a touch.

No matter how hard they try, they can’t resist giving into their forbidden desires.

Even if it costs them everything.

4 stars

“I’m never going to stop being me, Kai, and I don’t want you to stop being you. So how can we be together when we belong to separate worlds?”
“By building one of our own,” I said simply.


Alexa, play “London Boy” by Taylor Swift.

This book was something different from what Ana usually writes, and I loved it. Ana is famous for her steamy billionaire romance stories and swoon-worthy, morally grey characters. But I loved how she stepped outside her usual style and gave us this opposites-attract, steamy romance with utterly charming characters. It was addicting from the very start because of how opposite Isa and Kai were. They weren’t supposed to fall for each other due to the forbidden nature of their relationship.

“Still, there was something about her that drew me in like a siren calling to a sailor. Destructive, certainly, but so beautiful it would almost be worth it.”


I loved how sweet and beautiful this story was, with its perfectly portrayed characters. The romance was refreshing—healthy, alluring, and without lies or betrayals. One thing I love about Ana’s books is how she writes her Asian characters the way they should be written—flawed yet perfect in their own way. She perfectly captured Asian culture and families in this book. Both MCs are Asian, and I loved how similar their cultures and family dynamics were, yet so different at the same time.

Isabella Valencia is bold, impulsive, and sassy. She’s the complete opposite of Kai, with her flamboyant and vibrant personality. But she’s also kind and thoughtful, and she believes she doesn’t deserve happiness because of what happened in her past with her ex. She struggles with writer’s block in this book, and Kai is always there to help her through it. I’m so glad she found both love and her dream in the end.

“She shone too brightly for the dark, traditional confines of Valhalla.”


Kai Young is the epitome of aristocratic sophistication. And the fact that he’s an Asian Brit who wears glasses, loves books, translates them into Latin for relaxation, and turns into a territorial caveman when he’s jealous? He’s just so hot, charming, and perfect. But beyond that, he’s thoughtful and caring, with a soft spot for only Isa. He’s very different from other MMCs in Ana’s books—he’s not morally grey and would rather handle things in a civilised way… though not so civil when it comes to the bedroom. His British accent and the way he calls Isa love and my love are the only things keeping me sane in this life.

“I’d never fallen in love before her. Once I did, I did it the way I did everything else. Completely. Totally. Irrevocably.”


I love how Isa and Kai are so different from each other yet never try to change one another. They are both unapologetically themselves. Isa is a social butterfly with purple-streaked hair, while Kai is confident and reserved in every way. But they found love amidst the secret libraries of Valhalla Club, their sparkling chemistry, and their undeniable tension. I adore their banter—especially how Isa had an apparent fetish for discussing sex in public just to fluster Kai, and how he never made her feel ashamed about it.

“You should’ve never let me take you, Isabella. Because now that I have, I won’t be able to let you go.”


They helped each other grow and pushed one another outside their comfort zones. I loved how they always communicated their feelings, never letting doubts creep in to destroy what they were building. They both had walls around them, yet they found a space between those walls and loved each other fiercely—flaws and all. It was beautiful how they fell in love despite everything and everyone against them. I love them so much!

“We’ve been through some dark times, but you were always the brightest part of my life. Even when we broke up. Even when I walked out. Just knowing you existed somewhere in this world was enough.”


There’s a completely useless third-act breakup, and I hated how Isabella broke Kai’s heart. That man didn’t deserve that! But the ending was perfect, and I’m so glad their families accepted them. I’m beyond happy that Kai and Isa found each other, worked through their differences, and fell deeply in love.

4 —hottie with glasses— stars.

❛ There was something about her that drew me in like a siren calling to a sailor. Destructive, certainly, but so beautiful. ❜


It’s always enticing and thrilling to dive into a book or story written in not "the traditional" author’s style. A.H. Tiptoed out of her confort zone and painted a surprising and somehow refreshing healthy relationship lacking her usual penchant for lies, trahisons and people being killed left and right.

"We were opposites in almost every way, from our habits and hobbies to our temperaments and taste in books."

The story followed Isabella a bartender at the Valhalla —"an exclusive members-only society for the world’s rich and powerful,"—and accessory an aspiring thriller author. And Kai Young who was concurring for the C.E.O post at his family’s company. The two of them couldn’t be more polar opposites from each other. One was a purplehead with an outgoing personality and a too high to be elegant laugh and the other was a well tailored business man with glasses and a sophisticated British accent. So how and why the two of them ended together?

"He looked aristocratic, like a prince among commoners."

Kai Young is officially a new standard for paper boyfriends. His character was THE invigorating aspect of the storyline. He wasn’t a compulsive man with sociopath tenderizes, he was a charming and cultured man with such a kind and soft spot for Isabella. Everything he did, said was a perfection in their relationship. No wrong move from Kai Young! HE CARRIED THE BOOK!!

"she shone too brightly for the dark, traditional confines of Valhalla."

Isabella’s frivolous character and vivid personality were enjoyable for most of the storyline. The way her personage kept adding some surprising and little plot twists here and there brought some life and colors into the plot-line.

"I’d never fallen in love before her. Once I did, I did it the way I did everything else. Completely. Totally. Irrevocably."

Their relationship was sweetly orchestrated and their chemistry was undeniable. They learned how to orbite around one another gently without each of them imposing his or her personality. They navigated through their friendship and then their relationship with accepting their differences and finding some commun points. They communicated and shared. It was one of these relationships were both of them worked to deserve the other.💜

i feel like this book had no direction or was simply too... pedestrian/plain/bare/drama-free. Kai (H) is busy trying to win votes for the CEO position in his company. Isa (h) is struggling with her writter’s block. its (sorta) friends to lovers between them, and the only threat to their relationship is all external, meaning: (1) Kais mother doesnt approve of Isa; (2) theyre under scrutiny of cheap tabloids because theyre from different backgrounds. this conflict of parental blessing & social class disparity is sooo overused. im tired of it.

4.5 ⭐️ Okay wait… this was so much better than I expected!!

💜 The Premise

Isabella Valencia is a chaotic bartender at an ultra-exclusive club for the rich and powerful, trying to survive her shifts, push through writer’s block, and figure out her future.

Kai Young is reserved, disciplined, and impeccably put together. A billionaire heir under intense scrutiny, he thrives on control, routine, and maintaining his reputation as he competes for the role of CEO.

They are total opposites.
They absolutely should not get involved.
There’s also a strict no-fraternization rule…

…which they proceed to ignore.

🪶 My Thoughts

Kai and Isabella are complete contrasts—controlled vs spontaneous, proper vs free-spirited—and watching her slowly unravel his perfectly curated world was honestly my favorite part.

╰┈➤ Kai took me by surprise.

An intellectual billionaire with a British accent… and glasses?? Yeah.

But what really made him stand out is how soft he is for Isabella.

"You think you're broken, but I wish you could see yourself the way I see you. Smart. Strong. Beautiful. Imperfect by your own standards but so wonderfully perfect for me."

He’s attentive, reassuring, and unwavering in how much he believes in her—even when she can’t see it herself. The way he shows up for her, supports her, and gently pushes her to recognize her own potential was everything.

And then you add the jealousy, the possessiveness, and the whole ”only filthy for her” energy… I was DONE.

"That there's no going back after this." His admission was a warm breath on my skin. "You should've never let me take you, Isabella. Because now that I have, I won't be able to let you go."

╰┈➤ Isabella was just as compelling.

”She looked as out of place as a diamond among rocks. Not because she was a bartender in a room filled with billionaires, but because she shone too brightly for the dark, traditional confines of Valhalla.”

She comes across as bold, witty, and vibrant—purple hair, zero filter, inappropriate jokes—but underneath, she’s deeply insecure and struggling with feeling “behind” in life.

That internal conflict felt so real. The self-doubt, the fear of not being enough, the hesitation to trust herself—and the tendency to stay small even when it makes you unhappy… it hit hard.

╰┈➤ The Relationship

What I loved most is that they don’t try to change each other—they balance each other.

”Because she's beautiful, smart and funny. Because seeing her smile is like watching the sun rise, and being with her is the only time I feel alive. No other woman compares.”

Kai brings stability, comfort, and direction into her life, while Isabella brings warmth, spontaneity, and color into his.

They push each other out of their comfort zones in completely different ways—and it just works.

And the fact that this man was out here consulting neuroscientists to help her with writer’s block?? The standard is unreal.

"Admit it," I said around a mouthful of cheese and pepperoni. "You did have fun."
"Because of you."
Kai plucked a pepperoni off his slice and placed it on mine.

And yes—the feather scene???
The professor x schoolgirl 🥵

”Remember, you read a full page of Austen while getting spanked. If you can do that, you can do anything.”

╰┈➤ The Friendships

The girls’ dynamic felt even stronger in this book, and I loved seeing more of Alessandra and how she fits into the group. And the little Dante and Vivian crumbs?? So cute 🤭

"You were planning a surprise party for Vivian Russo on Coney Island?" Parker asked doubtfully.
A short but pregnant pause saturated the room.
"She likes Ferris wheels," Dante said. 😂

Tropes / What to Expect

💜 Opposites Attract
👀 Forbidden / Workplace Romance
💼 Billionaire Romance
💔 Third Act Breakup
🎧 Duet Narration

— Rating: 2.5 ★ .ᐟ

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ This book may have had the most unfunnily repetitive jokes known to man. King of Pride wasn’t necessarily bad, but it was definitely tedious. As much as I loved the mature, sophisticated atmosphere this series has, I’m starting to lose hope that it’ll be astonishingly better than the Twisted Series (which I wasn’t the biggest fan of.) With King of Wrath, the first book in the King of Sin series, the plot had its unexciting chapters but it was entertaining for the most part. This book though? It was rare that I got to a chapter that didn’t feel repetitive, the storyline as a whole was just so unmemorable and was far from being impactful. It wasn’t the worst book known to humankind, but it was far from being anything special. Maybe I’m starting this review off too harsh, King of Pride had its redeemable qualities, but there weren’t that many.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ I truthfully cannot remember an exciting point in the plot. Don’t get me wrong, it was decently entertaining while reading the book, yet I cannot recall any significant details besides the fact Isabella could not stop making dirty jokes whilst Kai was coincidentally nearby. I suppose there was the fact that both of the main character’s career conflicts were delved into but it honestly just made the plot more bland. There weren’t any huge plot twists or suspenseful moments that kept me enthralled, the entire time I couldn’t have cared less about Kai’s position as CEO or Isabella’s obsession with erotica. Unfortunately I could not tell you what the conflict was either because it was so boring, then said conflict only got more annoying when we got a lovely miscommunication trope shoved into the writing. The only semi-entertaining element was the forbidden romance due to Isabella’s job and Kai’s membership, so yay to that?

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ Isabella and Kai’s dynamic was okay, they had tons of tension and I loved how they balanced each other’s personality out. Yet they remained as unremarkable as the plot. I mean, they were definitely cute. Despite having little to nothing in common they connected deeply with one another which was enjoyable to see, you can’t go wrong with an opposites attract. Still, I’m unable to remember a singular exchange they had that felt impactful. They had their meaningful conversations with one another yet there were no genuine emotional stakes in any of them. Honestly, it could just be the tedious plot that made the characters’ relationship feel somewhat dull. They had decent banter and the chemistry between them felt like it was simmering beneath the surface throughout the entire book, but so many of their interactions just felt repetitive and it led to me being unable to really care for them. They did still have really cute interactions despite being repetitive!

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ This is one of the few books I felt that Ana Huang actually tried giving the main characters some individuality, but she unfortunately failed terribly. Don’t get me wrong, Isabella and Kai were sweet characters that I did enjoy reading about, but it felt like Isabella was a “not like other girls” girl while Kai was just sort of bland? They were definitely different from Ana’s usual main characters, but at the same time they weren’t characters I could connect with. Isabella had me annoyed with her unnecessarily large abundance of dirty talk while Kai just wasn’t really entertaining. They had somewhat interesting personalities, Isabella specifically had unique interests so I guess she did fulfill her role of not being like other girls. I did enjoy Kai’s sophisticated, straightforward personality paired with his bouts of sarcastic remarks, he may be one of the few Ana Huang MMC’s, within the Twisted and King of Sin series at least, whose whole personality wasn’t centered around being a dangerous grump. These details unfortunately still don’t erase that they weren’t outstanding main characters, they were cute and I didn’t dislike them despite some annoying features, but they also never stood out to me throughout the entire book.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ Asides from the tasteless plot and somewhat plain character dynamic, Ana Huang’s writing has undoubtedly improved in the sense of depictions and inner monologues. Unfortunately the cringey dialogue has made reappearances in King of Pride, thankfully in fewer amounts than prior books, but the story did have more enhancing and descriptive features to illustrate the settings. There wasn’t that much emotional depth and I truthfully couldn’t connect with the story at all, unfortunately any depth of the differing family problems for both main characters were interesting at first but slowly became unentertaining which had me zoning out whilst reading, however I have to appreciate Ana’s attempt at trying to incorporate unique features into her story. I love seeing the diversity in her characters and although her plots are getting repetitive, she certainly knows how to remember small details throughout the book and incorporate them into the plot in an exciting way.

౨ৎ Isabella Valencia.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ Everyone has their unique traits but why are we talking about glow in the dark condoms at our work place loudly enough for a passerby to hear? We love a girl who's confident in herself with the right amount of boldness, but at some points it felt like she just wanted attention for being “different”. Besides this aspect Isabella was an entertaining FMC, she had decent interests and hobbies that I’ve never read about in a character having prior which made her decently unique! I must say she had almost no depth despite this uniqueness. Her conflicts with writing were talked about, yet after a while how her problems were mentioned felt repetitive. She grew as a person but I feel her progress wasn’t described as thoroughly as it could have been. As interesting as she was I just couldn’t connect or relate to her. Not that every character has to be relatable, I just wish we had seen more depth. I definitely enjoyed her sweet personality and, like always, the scenes she shared with her friends were some of my favorites!

౨ৎ Kai Young.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎‎ He had some cute moments and I did enjoy his character, but his career/business storyline became confusing as the book went on and I feel like it made his character ten times more boring. Whether I found this storyline confusing because I’m not a business person or it wasn’t explained fully, who knows. It just became tedious to me at some point and I had to physically force myself to get through it so I could actually read about Isabella and Kai’s romance. As much as I liked him he was truthfully just another mediocre MMC that didn’t feel at all special. He was the one who made the banter between him and Isabella amusing with his honesty and aversion towards her brusque way of speaking, I love a blunt man, but regrettably he wasn’t all that memorable and didn’t make a true impact for me. He also got decent depth, nothing nearing astounding but I enjoyed seeing a look into his fears. I honestly don’t know… he wasn’t dislikable per say, just generically bland at times. I guess he did make me giggle at times?

⤿ read: may 07 - june 12 ; 2025
